wa_frog_prince.notes: SCOPE (report only): MP-only line (posted 2013, FA T. Ramier, 5.11c, trad), not in the Index guide's Lower Town Wall list. MP: start on Princely Ambitions P1, continue up and right where Princely hand-traverses left, end at the base of Tadpole (wa_tadpole). The guide's Tadpole teaser says Tadpole follows the first half of Princely and then goes straight up, so the guide appears to treat this lower section as the way into Tadpole; Frog Prince may be Tadpole's start under another name. Le Grande Bleu (wa_le_grande_bleu, context) climbs Model Worker and finishes on Frog Prince. Owner decides whether it stays its own row. No grade/length lock (one publisher, scope open). Bolts on the route (MP names a second bolt) but no count, so bolts not proposed. FA 'T. Ramier' matches MP only. No SAFETY issue found; this is the Dwarf Tossing section, not on or below Great Northern Slab, and no post-2023 change is reported.

wa_tadpole.notes: Own line. MP: directly above Model Worker (reached from it), or by rappel from the Newest Industry slab anchors; fingers, a crux past a pin, then a flaring offwidth/chimney corner. The guide's teaser starts it up the first half of Princely Ambitions and then straight up, which is the line MP calls Frog Prince (wa_frog_prince) for its lower part; both give 5.11c, so the grade lock stands, but the two publishers may draw the start differently (see Frog Prince). pitches 1 kept (no count stated). FA DEFECT (report only): fa stores 'Dave Anderson, John Teasdale. FFA P1: Terry Lien, Greg Olsen' (FA and FFA in one string, ffa empty); MP gives the same parties, no years; no second source. The 'FFA P1' label implies more than one pitch historically; not acted on. No SAFETY issue found.

wa_stern_farmer.notes: RELATION to Stern Farmer Full (wa_dwarf_tossing_to_narrow_arrow_stern_farmer_full): ONE line, not two. Stern Farmer was a two-pitch route: free P1 (this row, 5.12b, 75 ft to chains) and an A3+/C2 roof pitch above (cascadeclimbers 2007 aided it). MP's FA line credits P2 to Mike Schaeffer as one long pitch from the ground; MP's Stern Farmer Full page (posted 2024) says to continue past the Stern Farmer P1 anchor without clipping it, 165 ft, 5.12d PG13, FA Mikey Schaefer. So this row = P1 and Stern Farmer Full = the whole line freed in one pitch. Sushi Farmer branches off this pitch (see its row). Start is shared with Japanese Gardens (MP, guide, CC); the stored approach_variants baseFinding says the same. FA DEFECT (report only): fa stores 'FFA P1: Terry Lien, Tom Michael. P2: Mike Schaeffer (as one long pitch from the ground)' (FFA label and the P2 / full-line party in one string, ffa empty); the P2 party belongs to Stern Farmer Full, whose fa is null. Spelling Schaeffer (this row/MP FA line) vs Schaefer (MP Full page) differs within MP. SAFETY note (no stored-prose problem): MP calls the protection thin and reports several close calls and an injury. theCrag was Forbidden (one try).

wa_sushi_farmer.notes: SCOPE (report only): a VARIATION, MP-only (posted 2016, FA unknown), not in the Index guide's list. MP: start up Stern Farmer (wa_stern_farmer), step left to undercling the flake that is Japanese Gardens' final crux, then go straight up out of the dark corner onto an open face to chains; 115 ft (35 m), 5.12b/c; a #2 Camalot for the undercling plus a piece for the Japanese Gardens crux; warns of rope drag. So it shares its start with Stern Farmer (itself the Japanese Gardens start) and a crux with Japanese Gardens, with its own upper face and anchor. Not a pitch of Stern Farmer Full. Under the batch S rule (an MP-only variation is a catalog-defect candidate) only access is proposed and nothing is locked; stored 5.12b/c, 1 pitch, 35 m match MP. Owner decides.
